content_voiceover: This page reviews two exam favorites. First, treatment free remission, or TFR, in CML. The Taiwan guideline requires chronic phase disease, a high quality quantitative PCR lab, typical BCR-ABL1 transcripts like e13a2 or e14a2, and a sustained deep molecular response, more than three years for MR4 or more than two years for MR4.5, before attempting TKI discontinuation. The trap here is option C. Patients who fail first line TKI due to resistance and later achieve a deep response on second line therapy are not considered adequate TFR candidates, because failure implies an unstable, resistant clone even if it looks quiet now. Second, polycythemia vera management. Remember the ELN definitions of hydroxyurea resistance and intolerance. Leg ulcers that develop after starting hydroxyurea are explicitly classified as hydroxyurea intolerance, which is why the statement denying that link is the wrong one.
keypoints: TFR needs chronic phase, deep molecular response duration, and quality PCR
Resistance to first-line TKI disqualifies TFR even after later deep response
Hct target below 0.45 reduces vascular events in PV
Leg ulcers on hydroxyurea count as hydroxyurea intolerance
keypoint_voiceover: Key takeaways. TFR candidacy requires chronic phase disease, a validated PCR lab, and a documented deep molecular response held for at least two to three years. A history of TKI resistance, not just intolerance, generally excludes a patient from attempting discontinuation. For polycythemia vera, keep hematocrit under zero point four five to cut vascular risk, and remember that leg ulcers occurring on hydroxyurea are a recognized sign of drug intolerance, not a separate unrelated finding.
